summary: This Snowflake documentation page describes the AGGREGATE_QUERY_HISTORY Account Usage view, which tracks statement execution over time and aggregates repeated SQL statements in one-minute intervals. It is especially useful for monitoring Unistore workloads that run a small number of distinct statements at high throughput. The page lists the view's columns, explains the OBJECT statistics fields and the QUERY_PARAMETERIZED_HASH column, notes up to 180 minutes of latency, and gives example queries for errors, throughput, top queries by execution count, and latency analysis.
one_line: Snowflake Account Usage view that aggregates repeated query executions in one-minute intervals for workload monitoring and performance analysis.
key_facts: AGGREGATE_QUERY_HISTORY is an Account Usage view available to all accounts.
The view aggregates repeated SQL statements in one-minute intervals and contains similar data to the QUERY_HISTORY view.
AGGREGATE_QUERY_HISTORY is particularly useful for monitoring Unistore workloads that execute a small number of distinct statements repeatedly at high throughput.
The CALLS column gives the number of times the statement (query + query plan) was executed in the aggregation interval.
The QUERY_PARAMETERIZED_HASH column is a hash computed on the query after parameterizing all literals, so queries differing only in literals such as 'TIM' and 'AIHUA' share the same value.
Identifier, session variable and stage names are case insensitive for QUERY_PARAMETERIZED_HASH, and white space differences are ignored.
OBJECT-type statistics fields include sum, avg, stddev, min, median, p90, p99, p99.9 and max across all executions within the aggregation interval.
The PERCENTAGE_SCANNED_FROM_CACHE value ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 and must be multiplied by 100 to get a true percentage.
The ERRORS column lists error codes and messages in the format {"code": "code1", "message": "msg1", "count": 10}.
TOTAL_ELAPSED_TIME is the elapsed time in milliseconds.
The usage notes state that latency for the view may be up to 180 minutes (3 hours).
The errors and hybrid table throttling example monitors TRANSACTION_BLOCKED_TIME, QUEUED_PROVISIONING_TIME, QUEUED_REPAIR_TIME, QUEUED_OVERLOAD_TIME and HYBRID_TABLE_REQUESTS_THROTTLED_COUNT.
The throughput example computes queries per second as SUM(calls) / 60 for the warehouse MY_WAREHOUSE.
The top-queries example ranks query_parameterized_hash values by SUM(calls) as execution_count in descending order.
